deployed_signal: swing ensemble (LightGBM LambdaRank + LightGBM regression + ridge)
verdict: The deployed swing ensemble ranked stocks with a mean daily rank IC of 0.033 (t = 3.7 after correcting for overlapping labels) across 14 out-of-sample years; plain 12-1 momentum managed 0.014. The edge was not steady: IC was negative in 2026. As a top-10 book rebuilt weekly with Indian delivery costs it returned 25.4% a year against 17.6% for an equal-weight portfolio of the same universe, with a worst drawdown of -33% against -38%. Costs took about 4.8% a year. Absolute returns are flattered by survivorship: an equal-weight portfolio of today's NIFTY 100 shows 23% a year; restricting each date to the stocks that were most liquid at the time brings it to 18%, still above NIFTY's 11% (a price index, without dividends). Judge the models by their margin over equal-weight, not their absolute return. Volatility is far more forecastable than return: the best volatility model (garch) cut forecast loss by 23% against trailing one-month volatility. The regime overlay changed the top-10 book's worst drawdown from -33% to -25% and its return from 25.4% to 18.7% a year. Of the deep networks (LSTM, GRU, temporal CNN, transformer), the best was TCN with an IC of 0.037, which beat the LightGBM ensemble's 0.033; as a top-10 book it returned 22.4% a year (Sharpe 1.14) against the ensemble's 25.4% (Sharpe 1.27). Blending the two lifted the IC to 0.040 but returned 24.7% a year, so the LightGBM ensemble stays the deployed signal: a better ranking statistic did not become a better portfolio after costs. These are research signals for paper trading. They are not investment advice, and past out-of-sample results do not promise future returns.
